# Target Architecture Document > **IMPORTANT:** This is a **draft** architecture document. It must be reviewed and approved by the Architecture Review Board before any code generation. ## 1. Provenance - **Project ID:** `pb_src` - **Generated At:** 2026-08-12T09:21:06Z - **Status:** `draft` - **Frozen Version:** none - **Approved By:** none - **Approved At:** none - **Seed Modules (auto-selected, 5 of 21 available):** - `MOD-PDQS` (pdqs) – online/UI track, 56 artifacts - `MOD-SHARED` (Shared Services) – mixed track, 191 artifacts - `MOD-HOKAN` (hokan) – UI track, 53 artifacts - `MOD-PUBLIC` (public) – UI track, 49 artifacts - `MOD-MASTER` (master) – UI track, 47 artifacts - **Prompt Version:** `arch-1.0` - **Project Config SHA256:** `ebce460b5d8def466853a0eba39904a44a75a9ee95a75173997a940aa23ed061` - **Coverage:** online modules represented, batch track not covered, mixed track covered via SHARED; uncovered modules = none (all 21 available, 5 selected). --- ## 2. Purpose & Target Platform The target system modernizes a legacy VB6/PowerBuilder application into a cloud-native solution. **Target Platform** | Aspect | Technology / Environment | | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Frontend | React 18 / TypeScript 5 | | Backend | Java 21, Spring Boot 3 | | Batch | Spring Batch | | Infrastructure | AWS Cloud | | Database | PostgreSQL 16 | | Build | Maven (backend) + pnpm (frontend) | | Runtime | JDK 21 / Node 20 | **Technology Allowlist** (bounds all generated code) ``` Java 21, Spring Boot 3, Spring Web, Spring Data JPA, Hibernate, Spring Security (JWT), Spring Batch, Bean Validation, MapStruct, Flyway, React 18, TypeScript 5, Vite, Axios, PostgreSQL 16, Maven, pnpm, AWS ECS, AWS RDS, AWS API Gateway, AWS EventBridge, AWS Secrets Manager ``` --- ## 3. Architecture Style & Layering The declared architecture style is `microservices`, but the target **topology** is a **modular-monolith** – a single deployable unit. All design decisions (schema-per-module, in-process communication) reflect this modular-monolith approach. **Layers** | Layer ID | Name | Responsibility | Allowed Dependencies | | ----------- | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- | | ARC-LYR-001 | Presentation | React/TypeScript UI; no business logic. | ARC-LYR-002 (API) | | ARC-LYR-002 | API | REST controllers, request/response DTOs, JWT/RBAC enforcement. | ARC-LYR-003 (Application) | | ARC-LYR-003 | Application | Use-case services, transaction boundaries, orchestration. | ARC-LYR-004, ARC-LYR-005 | | ARC-LYR-004 | Domain | Entities, value objects, domain rules (framework-free). | (none) | | ARC-LYR-005 | Infrastructure | JPA repositories, external adapters, messaging. | ARC-LYR-004 (Domain) | **Layer Dependency Diagram** ```mermaid graph LR Presentation[Presentation
React/TS] --> API[API
REST Controllers, DTOs] API --> Application[Application
Use-case Services] Application --> Domain[Domain
Entities, Value Objects] Application --> Infrastructure[Infrastructure
JPA Repositories, Adapters] Infrastructure --> Domain ``` --- ## 4. Component-Type Catalog Every generated component follows a fixed location, naming convention, and template. | Component Type | Layer | Folder | Naming Convention | Template | | ----------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------- | | Controller | ARC-LYR-002 | `src/main/java/**/web` | `Controller` | `controller.tmpl` | | DTO | ARC-LYR-002 | `src/main/java/**/web/dto` | `Request` or `Response` | `dto.tmpl` | | Service | ARC-LYR-003 | `src/main/java/**/service` | `Service` | `service.tmpl` | | Entity | ARC-LYR-004 | `src/main/java/**/domain` | `` | `entity.tmpl` | | Repository | ARC-LYR-005 | `src/main/java/**/repository` | `Repository` | `repository.tmpl` | | Mapper | ARC-LYR-003 | `src/main/java/**/mapper` | `Mapper` | `mapper.tmpl` | | ReactComponent | ARC-LYR-001 | `web/src/features/` | `.tsx` | `react_component.tmpl` | | ApiClient | ARC-LYR-001 | `web/src/api` | `Api.ts` | `api_client.tmpl` | --- ## 5. Data Architecture - **Entities:** None defined. Feature evidence is empty, so no entity list, primary keys, relationships, or PII flags are available. **All entity decisions remain unresolved and are low-confidence.** - **Persistence:** Spring Data JPA / Hibernate (PostgreSQL 16). - **Transaction Boundaries:** Per Application-service use case – Spring `@Transactional` at the service method level. - **Schema Strategy:** Schema-per-module within a single PostgreSQL database; no cross-module table access allowed. --- ## 6. Integration & Context Map ### Layer Dependencies *(Diagram already provided in Section 3.)* ### Module Integration Contracts All inter-module communication is synchronous REST (in-process within the monolith). The following Mermaid diagram shows the directed relationships (edges weighted according to the integration weight in the JSON). Module boundaries are enforced: modules never access another module’s tables directly; they call the target module’s service interfaces. ```mermaid graph LR debug --> syohin hokan --> public syohin --> public zaiko --> public hokan --> syohin tana --> public tana --> syohin app_labo_stock --> hokan master --> public keijyo --> syohin keijyo --> public zaiko --> syohin app_labo_stock --> tana pdqs --> syohin haraidashi --> public ido[Inventory Transfer] --> public tana --> mail teisei --> public app_labo_stock --> pdqs master --> syohin iraiden --> mail app_labo_stock --> azuhara app_labo_stock --> iraiden app_labo_stock --> keijyo azuhara --> haraidashi azuhara --> ido azuhara --> syohin azuhara --> mail azuhara --> teisei haraidashi --> syohin ido --> syohin iraiden --> syohin tanka --> syohin teisei --> syohin app_labo_stock --> debug app_labo_stock --> master app_labo_stock --> haraidashi app_labo_stock --> ido app_labo_stock --> syohin app_labo_stock --> tanka app_labo_stock --> teisei ances --> app_labo_stock public --> syohin master --> pdqs ances --> syohin hokan --> debug ido --> haraidashi iraiden --> azuhara iraiden --> public iraiden --> haraidashi public --> pdqs syohin --> pdqs tanka --> public teisei --> haraidashi teisei --> ido ``` *Node labels: `ido` = Inventory Transfer Shipment Management. All edges are REST calls.* --- ## 7. Cross-Cutting Concerns | Concern | Approach | |-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | Security | Spring Security with JWT bearer tokens; method-level `@PreAuthorize` for RBAC enforcement. | | Logging | SLF4J + structured JSON logs; correlation id attached to every request. | | Error Handling | `@ControllerAdvice` returning RFC 7807 Problem+JSON. | | Transactions | Spring `@Transactional` at the Application‑service boundary. | | Configuration | Spring profiles + externalized config; secrets from AWS Secrets Manager. | | Validation | Bean Validation annotations on request DTOs. | --- ## 7b. System Architecture (Tier B) ### Topology **Modular-monolith** – a single Spring Boot deployable containing all business modules. This maximises simplicity, preserves module isolation, and allows future extraction into microservices if needed. The `microservices` style declaration is overridden by concrete topology decisions. ### Data Ownership Schema-per-module within a single PostgreSQL instance. No cross-module table access is permitted; all inter-module calls go through the target module’s service interface (REST). This enforces bounded contexts at the data layer. ### Identity & Authentication - **Issuer:** In-app Auth module (login/refresh/logout) issuing JWTs (access + refresh tokens). - **RBAC source:** Legacy System Administration module (users, roles, permissions) – must be migrated/re‑implemented. - **Password migration:** Gradual – on first successful login after cutover, legacy passwords are re‑hashed with BCrypt. Accounts inactive for >90 days require a password reset. ### Configuration & Secrets - **Config:** Spring profiles and externalized properties. - **Secrets:** AWS Secrets Manager. ### Deployment & Runtime - **Packaging:** Single Spring Boot container + static React bundle. - **CI Pipeline:** Build → Test → Containerize. - **Infrastructure as code:** AWS ECS service + RDS (PostgreSQL) baseline. - **Environments:** `dev`, `stage`, `prod`. ### Data Migration & Cutover - **Approach:** One-time ETL from legacy DB to PostgreSQL, using per‑entity field mapping specifications derived from the legacy data dictionary. - **Cutover:** Freeze‑and‑migrate with validation reconciliation. **HIGH‑RISK – human‑gated.** Requires dry‑run, rollback plan, and explicit approval. ### Observability - **Logging:** SLF4J structured JSON + correlation ID. - **Metrics:** Limited to Spring Boot Actuator health/metrics endpoints. Micrometer and CloudWatch are **not in the tech allowlist** – decision escalated. - **Tracing:** In‑process (single deployable); distributed tracing will be added only if services are later extracted. - **Health:** Actuator health endpoint enabled. ### Testing & Acceptance Gate - **Unit:** JUnit 5. - **Integration:** Testcontainers (PostgreSQL) to avoid JPA connection issues. - **Acceptance gate:** Application compiles, boots green, smoke and API/contract tests pass. ### Concurrency - **Optimistic locking** via JPA `@Version` on all editable entities. ### Audit - **Enabled** – planned with Hibernate Envers or custom audit tables per module, recording who changed what and when. ### Decision Ledger Summary The architecture was derived autonomously. The following decisions are **escalated** and reserved for the human review‑by‑exception gate: | Decision ID | Area | Decision | Confidence | Escalated | |-------------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|-----------| | DL-003 | Data Ownership | Schema‑per‑module, no cross‑module table access | high | **yes** | | DL-004 | Identity | In‑app JWT issuer, RBAC from legacy, BCrypt migration | medium | **yes** | | DL-007 | Data Migration | One‑time ETL, freeze‑and‑migrate | low | **yes** | | DL-008 | Observability | Only Actuator metrics (Micrometer/CloudWatch not in allowlist) | low | **yes** | Non‑escalated decisions (DL-005, DL-006, DL-009, DL-010, DL-011) are still part of the ledger but do not require special review. --- ## 8. Non-Functional Requirements | Category | Target | Architectural Response | |--------------|----------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------| | Performance | p95 API latency < 300 ms | Stateless services, connection pooling, read models where needed. | | Availability | 99.9% | Multi‑AZ ECS, health checks, graceful shutdown. | | Security | No unauthenticated write paths | JWT/RBAC enforced at the API layer (method‑level `@PreAuthorize`). | --- ## 9. Code Generation per Feature ### Codegen Directives - **Element-to-Component Mapping:** Empty – no feature elements exist, so no concrete mapping is available. - **API Conventions** - Base path: `/api/v1` - Versioning: path‑based (v1 implicit) - Pagination: **not specified** – see open question ARC‑OQ‑002 - Error model: RFC 7807 Problem+JSON via `@ControllerAdvice` - Standard HTTP status codes: 200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 422, 500 - DTO rules: Bean Validation on request DTOs; MapStruct for entity ↔ DTO mapping - **Security Rules** Applies to all state‑changing endpoints (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE): JWT authentication with method‑level `@PreAuthorize` enforcing appropriate RBAC role. - **Legacy Pattern Map** - PowerBuilder DataWindow → RESTful endpoint (Spring Web) backed by JPA repository - Embedded SQL (VB6/PowerBuilder) → JPQL / derived queries in Spring Data JPA - Transaction Object (PowerBuilder) → Spring `@Transactional` - OLE/DLL bridge calls → REST API calls via `RestTemplate`/`WebClient` - Global module state → stateless, injected configuration/Spring Service - **Dependency Rules** (enforced strictly) - Presentation → API - API → Application - Application → Domain - Application → Infrastructure - Infrastructure → Domain - Domain must not depend on any outer layer - **Coverage:** Seed feature total = 0; no mappings to cover. ### Per-Feature Export Bundle For each feature to be generated, the downstream generator receives an export bundle containing: 1. This **frozen architecture document**. 2. The feature’s **SRS** (software requirements specification). 3. The feature’s **story** (user story / use case). 4. **Related legacy source files** (VB6/PowerBuilder) for the feature. 5. The feature’s **domain slice** definition (bounded context from the module manifest). The architecture is generated **once** and reused for every feature, ensuring generated code composes consistently across the entire application. --- ## 10. Assumptions & Open Questions The following items remain unresolved and **must be addressed by the Architecture Review Board** before code generation can proceed. | ID | Question | Impact | |-----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | ARC-OQ-001 | Feature evidence is empty; no operations, screens, or data structures provided. How were features selected for seed modules? | Cannot derive entities, element‑to‑component mapping, or confirm API contracts. Architecture derivation is placeholder. | | ARC-OQ-002 | Pagination requirements (default/max page size, sorting) are unspecified. | API responses may suffer from unbounded result sets and inconsistent pagination. | | ARC-OQ-003 | Batch strategy is defined but no batch‑track modules or features are present in evidence. | Batch jobs may be generated with no specification; could be incomplete or misaligned with legacy schedules. | | ARC-OQ-004 | RBAC roles and specific permission assignments are not defined in evidence. | Only a generic RBAC rule can be applied; role names and per‑endpoint granularity remain unknown. | | ARC-OQ-005 | Glossary of domain terms is empty; module descriptions are provisional or auto‑generated. | Entity and field naming may not reflect actual business semantics, causing mismatches with legacy. | | ARC-OQ-006 | Observability approach references Micrometer and CloudWatch, but neither appears in the tech_allowlist. | Required monitoring infrastructure may not be implementable; potential compliance gap. | | ARC-OQ-007 | Skeleton declares architecture_style='microservices' but topology='modular-monolith'; all decisions describe a monolith. | Code generation may inconsistently produce either distributed or monolithic artifacts. | **Low-Confidence Architectural Items** - Data architecture entities (entirely absent) - Identity migration approach (DL-004, confidence: medium) - Observability implementation (DL-008, confidence: low) - Data migration plan (DL-007, confidence: low) All **escalated decisions** (DL‑003, DL‑004, DL‑007, DL‑008) require explicit human approval before code generation.
